sections.html:
Rome sits in Oneida County in central New York and shares the Utica-Rome metro area with Utica. At 75.7 square miles it ranks second among New York cities by area, so density is low, about 429.2 people per square mile. The 2020 population of 32,127 has slipped 1.4 percent, to an estimated 31,682.

The city's ZIP codes include 13440, 13441 and 13442, plus 13308 for Blossvale and 13478 for Verona, so confirm the municipality on your deed and tax bill before you list. Houses of very different ages sit inside one city boundary, and a buyer's first question is usually when the house was built and what has been replaced since.

A typical Rome home is valued at $154,400, and 56.6 percent of households are owners. Rent runs $909, and household income at the midpoint is $59,925.

  • 13,870 households averaging 2.13 people.
  • Owner costs of $1,431 a month with a loan and $701 with none.

At that price level a major repair is a large share of a house's value, so owners sometimes weigh an as-is sale against fixing up first.

Winters are the main stress on a house here, with about 102 inches of snow in an average year and January lows averaging 12.9 degrees. A tornado rated EF2 hit the center of the city on July 16, 2024, damaged roofs and brick buildings, and prompted emergency declarations from the city, county and state. If your house was damaged then, keep repair invoices, permits and insurance paperwork together to hand to a buyer.

sections.h2: Permits for work on a house
sections.html:
Rome's Code Enforcement office issues building permits and inspects work under the state's Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code. Call the office whenever you are not sure a project needs a permit.

  • Permits are generally required for new windows, kitchen and bath remodels, decks, porches and steps, pools, chimney work and any plumbing or electrical change.
  • A stop work order is issued to any job started without a permit, and fees double for work that began first.
  • Accessory structures under 144 square feet need a permit but carry no fee.
  • All plumbing must be done by a plumber holding a City of Rome license.

Pools holding 24 inches of water or more need a permit, and a pool without its electrical inspection cannot get a Certificate of Compliance. Housing inspectors assigned to each ward handle property maintenance and zoning enforcement, and multiple dwellings of three units or more get fire safety and property maintenance inspections at least every three years.

sections.h2: When Rome property taxes are due
sections.html:
Rome's city treasurer collects city, school and county taxes on a set calendar, and city taxes may include water, sewer and refuse charges.

City of Rome property tax due dates
Due dateWhat is due
January 31Metered water and sewer, special assessments
February 28County tax
April 30City tax first half, school tax second half
July 31Metered water and sewer
October 31City tax second half, school tax first half

The Treasurer's Office, in City Hall at 198 North Washington Street, can send a duplicate bill at 315-339-7689. On the assessment side, grievance day falls on the first Tuesday in August.

sections.h2: The assessor's stamp on a deed
sections.html:
Rome has one extra step before the county will take a deed. The Oneida County Clerk requires the deed itself to be stamped by the Rome City Assessor first, at 198 North Washington Street, Suite 1B (315-339-7614). Allow time for that stop before your closing date.

The clerk's land recording page then lists a $45 statutory fee, $5 for each page, a $5 TP-584 filing fee and a $125 real property transfer report fee for residential property. A deed needs a legal description, the full names and physical addresses of both parties, and original notarized signatures. White-out or redaction means rejection. If you must correct an error, the clerk suggests drawing a new deed.

sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a Rome house?
sections.html:
Hiring an agent, selling on your own and taking a cash bid are the choices. With the midpoint home near $154,000, repair bills, a vacant house through a Rome winter and a sales commission each take a big bite of what you keep.

  • Choose an agent when the house shows well and you are happy to wait on a buyer's loan.
  • Choose a sale by owner if you will manage the Property Condition Disclosure Statement and the contract yourself.
  • Price out a cash bid for a home with postponed repairs, storm damage, tenants or a probate matter.

Hand the state disclosure statement to the buyer before a contract is signed. Late or missing delivery means a $500 price credit for the buyer.

Rome's local steps add up, so line them up before an offer arrives. Ask Code Enforcement whether any permit for past work was left open, especially windows, decks, porches or a pool. Find the most recent city, school and county bills, and call the Treasurer's Office if one never arrived. Set aside time for the assessor's stamp on the deed, then file at the Oneida County Clerk.

A cash sale does not wait on a lender's appraisal, so these steps are usually what sets the pace. If the house is in probate or has tenants, say so at the start, since it changes who has to sign and when the house can be shown.

sections.h2: Taxes and water when you sell mid-year
sections.html:
Because Rome's calendar mixes city, school and county taxes, a sale rarely lands neatly between bills. The city tax and the school tax each run in two halves, April 30 and October 31, but the halves are swapped: April 30 carries the city's first half and the school's second half, while October 31 carries the city's second half and the school's first. County tax is due February 28. Metered water and sewer are billed on January 31 and July 31.

Ask your closing attorney to work out in writing which of these are paid and which fall to the buyer. Special assessments and metered water charges can ride on the January 31 bill, so a final water reading is worth requesting before the keys change hands. If any bill is unpaid at closing, it comes out of your proceeds, which is easier to handle when the Treasurer's Office has given you the exact balance beforehand. Keep copies of every payment receipt in the same folder as the bills, because the buyer's attorney may ask to see them.

faqs.q: Does a Rome deed need a stamp from the city assessor?
faqs.a: Yes. The Oneida County Clerk requires deeds for Rome properties to be stamped by the Rome City Assessor before recording. Allow time for that step before closing.

faqs.q: Does the 2024 tornado affect how I sell a Rome house?
faqs.a: It can. An EF2 tornado crossed the city on July 16, 2024, and damaged roofs and brick buildings. Keep repair invoices and permits to show a buyer.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a Rome address?
faqs.a: The Rome City School District covers most of the city and runs Rome Free Academy. Oriskany, Sherrill and Westmoreland districts cover other parts, so look at the tax bill.

faqs.q: Whom do I contact if a Rome tax bill never arrives?
faqs.a: Call the City Treasurer's Office at 315-339-7689 for a duplicate. Checks go to the City of Rome at 198 North Washington Street.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for window replacement in Rome?
faqs.a: Generally yes. New windows are among the work that needs a permit because of energy code and egress rules, and doubled fees apply if work starts first.
